dimensions.assessment: Affects the President, the Department of Justice Pardon Attorney, future recipients of presidential pardons, and federal election committees.
dimensions.evidence: A person who has received a pardon from the President may not make, in the determination of the Federal Election Commission, any contribution in an amount greater than $1,000

dimensions.assessment: Requires DOJ submission of criminal history and recidivism analysis for pardons to Congress and caps political donations by pardon recipients at $1,000.
dimensions.evidence: the Pardon Attorney of the Department of Justice shall submit to Congress within 30 days after such a grant a written analysis of any criminal history

dimensions.assessment: The source does not state or imply specific federal spending or revenue changes.
Imposes new reporting requirements on the Department of Justice and amends campaign finance restrictions regarding presidential clemency recipients.
dimensions.evidence: In the case of any pardon by the President, the Pardon Attorney of the Department of Justice shall submit to Congress within 30 days after such a grant a written analysis

dimensions.assessment: Enacts permanent statutory requirements governing all future presidential pardons and related campaign contributions.

missing_information: Administrative costs for the Department of Justice to compile the required congressional reports.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill places disclosure requirements on presidential pardons through the Department of Justice and imposes contribution limits on pardon recipients contributing to the President's authorized committees, leadership PACs, or independent expenditure entities.
